name: Mr. Restori
role: Brings back what is gone — careful as a restorer in white gloves
greet.1: Piano, piano — first let's see what exactly is missing.
greet.2: Which state do you want? I'll bring it back as it was.
greet.3: White gloves on. Nothing that is still there gets overwritten without asking.
fire_note: Mr. Backupsy's backups stay exactly as they are — I only read them.

fit.packages.one: Mr. Backupsy's packages hold 1 app or VM I can bring back.
fit.packages.other: Mr. Backupsy's packages hold {n} apps and VMs I can bring back.

fit.no_packages: Mr. Backupsy is set up, but there are no packages yet — they come with his next backup run. Then I can bring apps and VMs back.
fit.with_backup: Nothing for me to bring back yet: I bring apps and VMs back from Mr. Backupsy's packages and their snapshots, and there are none so far. Worth hiring together with him.
fit.nothing: Neither packages nor snapshots on this server — there's nothing for me to bring back yet.
bubble.no_engine: Mr. Backupsy's engine isn't there — so there are no packages for me to read.
bubble.asleep: The disk with Mr. Backupsy's packages is asleep — I won't wake it.
bubble.no_packages: No packages yet: they come with Mr. Backupsy's first backup run.
bubble.ready: {apps} apps and {vms} VMs can come back — the newest packages are from {when}.

bubble.gone.one: 1 of them is no longer on this server.
bubble.gone.other: {n} of them are no longer on this server.

notice.no_engine: Mr. Backupsy's backup engine isn't there. Without it there are no packages — only the local snapshots, which Ms. Snapshotini shows.
notice.no_place: Mr. Backupsy has no backup place yet (Set up… → Basics). The packages of the apps and VMs will lie there.
notice.asleep: The backup place ({path}) lies on a disk that is asleep. I show what I read before and don't wake it.
notice.no_packages: No packages in {path} yet — Mr. Backupsy writes them with every backup run.
help.tiles_text: Apps, VMs, databases, Kopia, the journal and «onto a new server»: a click opens that part, a second click closes it again.
help.row_text: One app or VM. A click anywhere on the row unfolds what can come back from where: from its package, from the local snapshots of its folders, from Kopia.
help.package_text: What Mr. Backupsy keeps per app and VM in the backup place: templates or compose files, database dumps, a media server's database copies; for a VM its XML, UEFI variables and TPM state. Earlier nights' packages lie in the snapshots of the backup place's share.
help.snapshots_text: The ZFS and btrfs snapshots that hold the folders of an app or VM (and whole shares it binds), with the newest date. A share on several pools and disks is the sum of its parts: a snapshot taken on all of them at once (Mr. Backupsy's) brings back all of it, one taken on some only brings back those parts — I say which. What comes back goes onto the share (/mnt/user/…), so Unraid places it by the share's settings. Only awake disks are looked at — a sleeping one only when you tick «wake» in a restore: then I wake it and wait until it answers.
help.kopia_text: When Kopia last copied the app or VM offsite — its own source (.apps/…, .vms/…) or its share's.
help.commands_text: Ready-made commands with your names and paths, to run in a terminal on the server.
apps_sub: Per app: its package, the local snapshots of its folders and Kopia — with dates.
apps_none: No app packages in the backup place.
apps_no_packages: No packages yet — they come with Mr. Backupsy's first backup run.
apps_files: Single files from a snapshot: copy them out of the snapshot paths in the rows.
chip.stale_hint: Written by an earlier run ({when}): the app or VM is gone or no longer backed up. The package stays — it is never deleted.
chip.gone_hint: None of its containers is on this server any more — the package can bring its template or compose files back.
chip.snaps_hint: Local ZFS or btrfs snapshots that hold its folders.
chip.no_snaps_hint: No snapshot holds its folders — they lie on a file system without snapshots, or nobody takes any.
chip.snaps_asleep_hint: Its folders lie on a disk that is asleep — I didn't look.
chip.kopia_never_hint: The engine's history knows no good Kopia copy of it yet.
ct.missing: Not on this server any more. Image {image}, digest {digest}
pk_nothing: Its package holds only docker inspect — what the container was. Its data is in its folders.
db.title: Databases
db.text: Stop the app's other containers first (Nextcloud: its maintenance mode instead, see below) — only the database container runs. The command plays the dump in and overwrites what the database holds now. With the user and password variables the dump was made with.
db.kept_hint: The last run couldn't dump it (failed, or the container wasn't running) — the last good dump stays in the package, from the date shown.
db.image_hint: The image the dump came from; digest {digest}
db.version: A database's folder from a snapshot only starts with the same major version of the image that wrote it (each package records image and digest); a dump also goes into a newer version.
db.pg_role: Postgres: errors like «role … already exists» while restoring are harmless — PostgreSQL's documentation says so.
db.alone: This database container stands on its own: stop the apps that use it first, wherever they are.
immich.title: Immich ({name}): restore into a fresh database
immich.s1_text: All of its containers except the database.
immich.s2_text: Immich wants a fresh database: stop the database container too, move its data folder aside (DB_DATA_LOCATION in the stack's .env, also in the package: {env}) and create it again empty. Move it, don't delete it, until Immich runs again.
immich.s3_text: Wait until its log says «ready to accept connections».
immich.s4: 4. Play the dump back (through Immich's sed, otherwise its vector extensions break)
immich.web: Immich can also do it itself: Administration → Maintenance → Restore database backup, from its own automatic database backups in UPLOAD_LOCATION/backups.
nc.title: Nextcloud ({name}): maintenance mode around the restore
nc.s2_text: Its data folder should come from the same night's snapshot, so files and database match.
nc.s4: 4. Only if the backup is older than what the sync clients have
nc.s4_text: A new data fingerprint tells the desktop and phone clients that the server went back in time — they upload their newer files instead of deleting them; the scan brings the database in line with the files.
sq.title: The media server's databases
sq.text: Emby, Jellyfin and Plex keep running during the snapshot, so their databases in it are only crash-consistent. The package holds a consistent copy made while they ran. It goes back with the server stopped; the -wal and -shm files next to the database belong to the state it replaces and are removed. Restore the copies of one server together.
sq.checked_hint: SQLite's quick_check found the copy in order.
sq.unchecked_hint: Unraid's sqlite3 couldn't check it — the server uses SQLite extensions of its own (Plex does). The copy was still made with SQLite's backup API.
sq.kept_hint: The last run couldn't copy the database (failed, too slow, or its disk was asleep) — the last good copy stays in the package, from the date shown.
sq.after: Its whole folder from a snapshot works too: stop the server, copy the folder back, start it — crash-consistent, like after a power cut, which SQLite usually copes with.
now.same_hint: The file on the server is exactly the one in the package.
now.differs_hint: The server has this file, but not as in the package — changed since, or a newer state. Nothing to restore unless you want the package's state.
now.missing_hint: The server doesn't have this file — it can come back from the package.
tpl.title: Unraid templates
tpl.text: Unraid's Docker page reads them from {dir}. Missing ones come back with the command; one that differs stays as it is.
tpl.after: Then Docker → Add Container → choose the template under «User templates»: Unraid creates the container and fetches the image again.
cmp.title: Compose files
cmp.text: The Compose Manager's project folder {dir}. Missing files come back with the command; existing ones are left as they are.
cmp.no_dir: The stack wasn't in the Compose Manager when it was packed — its files lie in the package's compose-files/.
cmp.indirect: An «indirect» stack points to its folder in a share — that comes back with the share; its compose files are in the package too (compose-files/).
cmp.after: Then Compose Manager → the stack → Compose Up: Docker fetches the images again.

earlier.title.one: Earlier nights (in 1 snapshot of the backup place)
earlier.title.other: Earlier nights (in {n} snapshots of the backup place)

earlier.text: The package as earlier nights left it — the commands work with these paths too.
earlier.none: No earlier package in the snapshots of the backup place — only tonight's.
snaps.text: The folders it keeps its data in, and the snapshots that hold them.
snaps.none: None of its containers binds a folder in a share.
snaps.missing_hint: This folder isn't on the server any more — it can come back from a snapshot or Kopia.
snaps.asleep_hint: This disk is asleep — I didn't look into it.
snaps.own_ds_hint: The folder is a ZFS dataset of its own: its snapshots belong to it alone.
snaps.inner_hint: Datasets of their own inside this folder ({list}) — a copy from this snapshot shows them empty; each has its own snapshots.
snaps.look: Newest state to look at or copy from:

snaps.whole.one: The whole share {share} — {names} binds it as it is. All of it can come back, or chosen entries at its top.
snaps.whole.other: The whole share {share} — {names} bind it as it is. All of it can come back, or chosen entries at its top.

snaps.whole_hint: A container binds this share as it is: its data is the whole share.
needs.title: Shares it needs
needs.text: Before its data comes back, these shares must be there — I never create a share; Unraid does.
needs.data_hint: The share is there and holds data — what comes back is copied next to it or swapped in.
needs.empty_hint: The share is there and empty — a restore goes straight in.
needs.missing_hint: The share isn't on this server — create it first in Unraid (Shares → Add Share).
needs.unknown_hint: Its disks are asleep — I didn't look whether it holds anything.
needs.create: Create it first in Unraid: Shares → Add Share, name {share} — then «Look again». Its data can come back only then.
needs.old: On the old server it was: {settings}.
needs.old_info: Only as information — choose what fits this server; its pools may be named differently.
needs.pools_missing: This server has no {names} — choose your own pools; those names are the old server's.
needs.old_none: Mr. Backupsy's package holds no settings of it.
needs.missing_button: The share {share} is missing — create it first in Unraid (Shares → Add Share).
needs.o_split: split only the top {level} directory levels
kp.none: Neither the app nor its shares go to Kopia.
kp.guide: How to get it out of Kopia →
own.title: The app's own backups — a second way
own.text: Some apps back themselves up. That's independent of Mr. Backupsy — and these folders are only in his backup if their share is.
own.asleep: its disk sleeps — not looked into
own.how.emby: Restore in Emby: the plugin's page in Emby's settings (Backup & Restore) → Restore. Into the same or a newer Emby.
own.how.jellyfin: Restore in Jellyfin (10.11 and newer): Dashboard → Backups → choose one → Restore.
own.how.plex: Plex writes these every three days. Stop Plex, copy the one you want over com.plexapp.plugins.library.db (remove its -wal and -shm next to it), start Plex.
own.how.immich: Immich writes a dump of its database every night (14 are kept). Restore in Immich: Administration → Maintenance → Restore database backup.
vms_sub: Per VM: its configuration in the package (XML, UEFI variables, TPM state), the snapshots of its disks, Kopia.
vms_none: No VM packages in the backup place.
vm.service_off: The VM service is off: libvirt.img isn't mounted, so I can't tell which VMs are defined right now.
vm.all: Everything back into libvirt.img — all VMs and networks from {when} ({size})
vm.all_text: For a lost or broken libvirt.img, or a new server: {file}
vm.all_1_text: Settings → VM Manager → Enable VMs: No. That unmounts libvirt.img. Is the image gone? Set it to Yes once — Unraid creates a new, empty one — then No again.
vm.all_2: 2. Unpack the archive into the image (in a terminal on the server)
vm.all_3_text: Settings → VM Manager → Enable VMs: Yes. All VMs are back with their UEFI variables and TPM state. Their disks must be where the XML says — on a new server, restore them first.
vm.state_hint: How libvirt sees it right now.
vm.missing_hint: libvirt doesn't know this VM any more — its package can define it again.
vm.unknown_hint: With the VM service off I can't tell whether it is defined.
vm.tpm_hint: Its package holds the virtual TPM's state — BitLocker and Windows Hello keep working after a restore.

vm.hostdev.one: 1 passed-through device (GPU, USB …) — it belongs to this server's hardware
vm.hostdev.other: {n} passed-through devices (GPU, USB …) — they belong to this server's hardware

vm.f_xml: its definition, as libvirt keeps it
vm.f_nvram_snap: UEFI variables of an Unraid VM snapshot
vm.f_snapdb: Unraid's list of its VM snapshots
vm.one: {name} back from its package (the other VMs keep running)
vm.one_text: With the VM service running, in a terminal on the server — this puts back {name}'s UEFI variables and TPM state from its package ({when}) and defines it again:
vm.one_after: It still exists: shut it down first, and only redefine it if you really want the package's state — virsh define changes the existing one.
vm.one_tpm: Its TPM state comes back too, so BitLocker and Windows Hello keep working.
vm.disks: Its disks must lie where the XML says: {list} — in brackets the snapshot of that night that holds them. Restore them first if they are gone.
vm.snaps: Only if its Unraid VM snapshots (the chain of disk files) come back too — their list and UEFI variables:
kopia_sub: The offsite copies: how to get something out, and which sources there are.
kg.off: Kopia is switched off in Mr. Backupsy's setup — there is no offsite copy. What comes back comes from the packages and the local snapshots.
kg.no_container: I can't find a Kopia container — install it first (with the same Container Path as before) and connect it to the repository.
kg.container: Kopia runs in the container {name}; it sees the snapshots under {root}.
kg.container_stopped: The container {name} is stopped — start it on Unraid's Docker page. It sees the snapshots under {root}.
kg.root_example: {root} is only an example: I couldn't read which Container Path your Kopia container gives the snapshots ({path}) — take the one from its template (Docker → kopia → Edit).
kg.s2: 2. Choose the source and the state
kg.s2_text: Snapshots → the source (the list below, all under {root}) → the snapshot of the date you want. Inside, every folder lies where it lies on the server.
kg.s3_text: «Download» gives single files or a folder as a zip in the browser. «Restore» writes into a folder of the container — the container only sees read-only paths, so map a writable folder for the time being: Docker → kopia → Edit → Add another Path, Container Path /restore, Host Path e.g. /mnt/user/<share>/restore, Access Mode Read/Write. Remove it again afterwards.
kg.s3_mapped: «Download» gives single files or a folder as a zip in the browser. «Restore» into {dest} — on the server that is {source}.
kg.s4_text: Look at what came back, then stop the app and copy it into place. Kopia writes as root, so give the files their old owner (chown --reference).
kg.password: Without the repository password nothing comes back from Kopia — not even through the provider. Keep it in a password manager and on paper.
kg.sources: The sources Kopia has, with the last good copy:
kg.own: Apps and VMs with a source of their own
move.title: Onto a new server
move.sub: If this server is gone (fire, theft, broken) or replaced: what comes back from where, what must not, and where it gets fiddly.
move.advisor: The Consultant has the installation guide for Kopia →
move.s1_text: Unraid 7.3 or newer, your licence (bound to the USB stick or the TPM — move it through your Unraid account), the array and the pools anew. Don't copy the old disk assignment or licence key over.
move.s2: 2. Create the shares under the same names

move.s2_text.one: Container templates and compose files point to /mnt/user/<share>. The share:
move.s2_text.other: Container templates and compose files point to /mnt/user/<share>. The {n} shares:

move.s2_cfg: Their old settings (pools, split level …) are in {path} for reference.
move.s2_needs: The shares the apps and VMs keep their data in, as they are on this server:
move.s3_text: Install the Kopia container with the same Container Path ({root}), connect it to the same repository with its password, and restore appdata, the backup place's share (the packages: templates, dumps, VM configurations) and the other shares — see «Kopia».
move.s3_nokopia: Kopia is off: there is no copy in Kopia — only what was on this server. Without it, only the local snapshots and dumps on surviving disks remain.
move.s4_text: Put the templates and stacks back (the commands below), then Docker → Add Container or Apps → Previous Apps. Docker fetches the images again (the packages name their versions and digests).
move.s4_after: Check fixed IPs on br0, own Docker networks, VLANs and passed-through devices (GPU) — they belong to the old server.
move.s4_indirect: A stack that is «indirect» points to its folder in a share — that comes back with the share; its compose files are in the package too (compose-files/).
move.s5_text: Start the database containers and play the dumps back — each app's row under «Apps» has the commands.
move.s5_nextcloud: Nextcloud: set the root of its data folder to www-data:users with 0750 (chown 33:100, chmod 0750), otherwise it refuses to work.
move.s6_offsite: Their disks go to Kopia with their share: restore them with Kopia, then their configuration (XML, NVRAM, TPM) — under «VMs».
move.s6_local: Their disks ({shares}) are only in local snapshots on this server — without this server they are gone. What remains is their configuration (XML, NVRAM, TPM) in the backup place, for VMs you install anew.
move.s6_xml: Adjust the XML on the new server: passed-through devices, CPU pinning, bridges, paths. A VM with Unraid VM snapshots has a chain of disk files (vdisk1.img + vdisk1.S…qcow2): copy all files of its folder.
move.s6_tpm: Virtual TPM: {names}. Windows may ask for its activation or the BitLocker recovery key after a change of hardware — keep those keys elsewhere.
move.s6_overlay: Switch the VM service on before restoring the configuration.
move.s7_snapshot: The flash goes to Kopia as its own source (_flash). Take only what you need from it: the settings of single plugins (config/plugins/<plugin>/), the go file, User Scripts.
move.s7_tar: The flash is in the archive {path}. Take only what you need from it: the settings of single plugins (config/plugins/<plugin>/), the go file, User Scripts.
move.s7_never: Never copy blindly: the disk assignment (super.dat), the licence key (*.key) and the network settings (network.cfg) belong to the old server.
move.s7_official: A whole flash comes back only the official way: Unraid's flash backup (a .zip, or the one in Unraid Connect) written onto a stick with the Unraid USB Flash Creator. From the office's copy take only single pieces — plugin settings, the go file, User Scripts.
move.s8_text: Install the Secretary Office plugin. Its data folder comes back with appdata (settings, history, Mr. Backupsy's settings.ini); then Mr. Backupsy → «Set up…» → Apply, so everything matches the new server.
fact.kopia: Knows the way out of Kopia
errors.restore_place_asleep: The backup place lies on a disk that is asleep — I won't wake it.
help.chips_text: Each row has two groups of chips. «Package» is what Mr. Backupsy keeps of it in the backup place (when it was written, and when Kopia took it along with the backup place's share). «Data» is its folders: their local snapshots, Kopia, and how they are protected. A package in Kopia doesn't mean the data is.
help.restoring_text: I bring things back myself. First you see exactly what I would do: the steps, what I put aside where (nothing is deleted), which containers stop and for how long. Only after «I have read what will happen» do I start — one restore at a time, and never while a backup, Mr. Backupsy's tour or the setup runs. While I restore, a backup run that comes along is skipped and says why.
help.journal_text: Every restore with its steps and what each found, what I put aside where, and the log. «Put back» undoes a restore (also one that failed): what I put aside goes back in its place, what I restored goes aside itself.
bubble.restoring: Piano, piano — I'm restoring {what}: step {n} of {total}.
bubble.busy_backup: A backup run holds the engine right now — I only read, I bring nothing back meanwhile.
bubble.busy_check: Mr. Backupsy is on his tour right now — I bring nothing back until he's done.
bubble.busy_dryrun: Mr. Backupsy is on a dry run right now — I bring nothing back until he's done.
bubble.busy_setup: Mr. Backupsy's setup is looking at the server — I bring nothing back until it's done.
bubble.busy_restore: Another restore holds the engine — one at a time.
bubble.busy_other: Someone holds the backup engine's lock — I bring nothing back until it is free.
notice.busy_backup: A backup run is going on: it holds the engine's lock, and I bring nothing back until it is done.
notice.busy_check: Mr. Backupsy is on his tour: I bring nothing back until he is done.
notice.busy_dryrun: Mr. Backupsy is on a dry run: I bring nothing back until he is done.
notice.busy_setup: Mr. Backupsy's setup holds the engine's lock: I bring nothing back until it is done.
notice.busy_restore: Another restore holds the engine's lock — one at a time.
notice.busy_other: Someone holds the backup engine's lock (state/lock): I bring nothing back until it is free.
chip.kopia_hint_all: Its own Kopia source holds its folders and its package: {source}
chip.kopia_hint_data: Its data goes to Kopia with its share: {source}
chip.kopia_hint_package: Its package goes to Kopia with the backup place's share: {source} — that says nothing about its data.
kp.covers_all: its own source — its folders and its package
kp.covers_package: the backup place's share — its package
cfg.button_hint: The templates and compose files that are missing or differ — what is there goes aside first. I never start or recreate a container.
vm.button_hint: Its XML, UEFI variables and TPM state — only while the VM is shut off.
rd.title.share: Restore the share {share} from a snapshot
rd.title.config: Restore the templates and compose files of {what}
rd.loading: Piano, piano — I'm looking at what exactly would happen …
rd.steps: What I will do, step by step
rd.aside: What I put aside first — nothing is deleted
rd.aside_none: Nothing is replaced, so nothing needs to go aside.
rd.measuring: Measuring the size in the background — a moment …
rd.sparse: Sparse files: they say {apparent}, but only {data} of it is data — the copy keeps the empty parts empty.
rd.failstop: If a step fails I stop there and touch nothing more; «Put back» then brings back the state before.
rd.confirm: I have read what will happen.
rd.started: {what}: I've started — the journal shows every step.
rd.wait_restore: A restore is going on — one at a time.
rd.part_uncovered_content: not in this snapshot — though it holds some of it now
rd.part_empty: nothing of it in this snapshot
rd.way_copy: Copy it next to the folder
rd.way_copy_hint: <folder>.restored-<time> — nothing is replaced, nothing stops. Take what you need from it.
rd.way_swap_hint: The copy is made first while everything runs; then what uses the folder stops for seconds, the folder goes aside as <folder>.aside-<time> and the copy takes its place.
rd.way_place_hint: Nothing is there to replace (an empty folder only goes aside): the copy is made first, then what uses it stops for seconds and the copy takes its place.
rd.wake: Wake the sleeping disk ({base}) to read it
rd.wake_hint: Only if you really need it — I never wake a disk on my own.
rd.waking: Waking {base} … a sleeping disk needs a few seconds, sometimes up to a minute, to spin up. Then I look into its snapshots.
rd.woke: {base} is awake now — Unraid lets it sleep again after its own delay.
kr.title: Restoring with me
kr.mapped: I restore into {dest} — on the server {source}: each time a folder of its own (<source>-<time>), from where it goes back by hand or with «Restore…» of the folder.
kr.none: The Kopia container has no writable folder for restores — the engine's mapping is read only, on purpose.
kr.how: Add one in Unraid: Docker → {name} → Edit → Add another Path, Container Path /restore, Host Path e.g. /mnt/user/<share>/restore, Access Mode Read/Write → Apply. I never change the container myself.
kr.loading: Asking Kopia for the snapshots of {source} …
kr.choose: Which snapshot do you want? Newest first.
kr.none_snaps: Kopia has no snapshot of this source.
kr.failed_hint: Kopia couldn't read these files or folders when it made this snapshot — they are not in it.
journal_sub: Every restore with its steps, what I put aside where, and how to put it back.
j.put_back_hint: This restore was undone with «Put back» — its journal is in the list too.
j.undone_aside: What this restore had brought back went aside:
j.undone_nothing: There was nothing of it left to put aside.
j.undone_entry: To the put back's entry in the journal
j.putback_hint: Undo it: what I put aside goes back in its place, what I restored goes aside itself.
j.no_putback: Nothing to put back: this restore replaced nothing.
j.no_putback_kopia: Nothing to put back: the restored folder stands next to everything else.
job.done.warnings: {what}: restored, with warnings — see the journal.
job.done.failed: {what}: not restored — see the journal. «Put back» brings back the state before.
step.dump: Safety dump of what the database in {container} holds now → {file}
step.ready: Wait until the database in {container} answers
step.play_immich: Play the dump into {container}, through Immich's documented search_path fix
step.verify: Check the tables of each database in {container} against the dump
step.fresh: Create {path} empty again, with the old one's owner and rights
step.undefine: Remove the definition of {name} (its disks, UEFI variables and TPM state stay)
step.vms_off: Make sure {names} are still shut off (their disks lie here) — if not, stop before anything is replaced
sn.exists: Something is already there: {path} — I never write over it.
sn.dump_failed: The safety dump of {container} didn't work — so I changed nothing.
sn.not_ready: The database in {container} didn't answer within {seconds} s.

sn.play_errors.one: 1 error while playing the dump (besides the expected «already exists») — see the journal.
sn.play_errors.other: {n} errors while playing the dump (besides the expected «already exists») — see the journal.

sn.verify_empty: No tables where the dump has some: {tables}
sn.verify_differs: Not as many tables as in the dump: {tables}
sn.verify_unread: The dump couldn't be read for the check.
sn.copy_vanished: Some files vanished while copying — the copy is still there.
sn.vm_running: A VM using it is running now: {names} — so I stopped before replacing anything. Shut it down (Unraid → VMs) and start again.
sn.nothing_there: Nothing there — nothing to put aside.
aside.safety_dump: A safety dump of what {from} holds now → {to}
aside.db_folder: The database's folder, as it is: {from} → {to}
why.mountpoint: it is a dataset with a mountpoint of its own
note.method_fresh: The fresh way: the database stops, its folder goes aside as it is, it starts on an empty folder and the dump goes in. PostgreSQL wants a full dump played into a fresh database like that, and the old one stays untouched aside — «Put back» swaps the folders back.
note.method_inplace_postgres: In place: the dump drops each of its databases and creates it anew. The safety dump is the way back.
note.method_inplace_mariadb: In place: the dump drops its database and creates it anew; users and rights stay as they are. The safety dump is the way back.
note.method_inplace_mongodb: In place: mongorestore --drop replaces each collection of the dump. The safety dump is the way back.
note.immich: Immich: only into a fresh database before the server starts, through its documented search_path fix — as Immich's own restore instructions say.
note.db_no_folder: Its folder can't be put aside ({why}) — so in place.
note.db_start: {container} is stopped — I start it for this.
note.db_stopped: {container} is stopped, so there is no safety dump — its folder goes aside as it is instead.
note.db_alone: This database container stands on its own: stop the apps that use it first, wherever they are.
note.dump_kept: The newest good dump is from {when} — the last run couldn't make one.
note.sqlite: The server stops for a few seconds; each database and its -wal and -shm go aside next to it, the copies take their place with the folder's owner.
note.files_copy: Nothing is replaced: the snapshot's state comes next to the folder.
note.files_swap: The copy is made while everything runs; then what uses the folder stops, the folder goes aside and the copy takes its place.
note.files_inner: Datasets of their own lie inside it ({list}) — the copy shows them empty; each comes back from its own snapshots.
note.files_part: The folder also lies elsewhere — this snapshot holds only the part on {base}.
note.files_parents: These containers see a folder above it and keep running: {names}.
note.files_vms_off: {names} keep their disks here and are shut off — leave them off until the restore is done; right before anything is replaced I look again.
note.files_share_empty: The share {share} is there and empty — it goes straight in; nothing needs to go aside.
note.files_place: Onto the share, {path} — Unraid places it by the share's settings: on {primary}.
note.files_place2: Onto the share, {path} — Unraid places it by the share's settings: primary storage {primary}, secondary {secondary}.
note.files_overflow: It doesn't all fit on {primary} above the share's minimum free space — Unraid puts the rest on {secondary}.
note.files_dataset: {path} is a ZFS dataset of its own on {base} — it comes back there, as a dataset.

note.files_dataset_snaps.one: Its snapshot stays with the dataset put aside ({dataset}) — the restored {path} starts without one. I still offer it for this folder, as «of the folder put aside».
note.files_dataset_snaps.other: Its {n} snapshots stay with the dataset put aside ({dataset}) — the restored {path} starts without any. I still offer them for this folder, as «of the folder put aside».

note.files_from_aside: This snapshot belongs to the dataset put aside earlier, {aside} — its state comes back here.
note.files_union: The share lies on several pools and disks — this snapshot's parts are put together: {bases}.
note.files_uncovered: This snapshot doesn't cover {bases}, where {names} holds something now — that part isn't in it (swapped in, it goes aside with the rest).
note.files_place_in: Nothing is there yet: the copy is made first, then it is moved into its place.
note.files_place_empty: Only an empty folder is there: it goes aside as {aside}, then the copy takes its place.
note.files_asleep: {base} is asleep — I didn't look whether it holds some of it too.
note.config: Only files that are missing or differ; what is there goes aside first. Nothing starts or is recreated — that's your click (below).

note.vm_hostdev.one: It has 1 passed-through device (GPU, USB …) — it must exist on this server.
note.vm_hostdev.other: It has {n} passed-through devices (GPU, USB …) — they must exist on this server.

note.kopia: Kopia writes into a folder of its own; nothing on the server is replaced.
after.nextcloud: Nextcloud: if the backup is older than what the sync clients have — docker exec -u {user} {container} php {occ} maintenance:data-fingerprint, then files:scan --all.
after.files_copy: The state lies in {path} — take what you need and delete it yourself when you're done; I never delete anything.
after.files_swap: The old folder stays in {aside} until you delete it — or «Put back».
after.files_empty_aside: The empty folder that was there lies in {aside} — delete it whenever you like.
after.tpl_apply: Docker → {container} → Edit → Apply: Unraid recreates the container with the restored template.
after.tpl_add: Docker → Add Container → Template: {template} → Apply: Unraid creates {container} and fetches its image.
after.compose_up: Compose Manager → {project} → Compose Up (or Update Stack).
after.vm_disks: Its disks must lie where the XML says: {list} — a folder comes back from a snapshot with «Restore…» under its snapshots (only while it is shut off).
after.vm_start: Start {name} on Unraid's VMs page when its disks are in place.
after.kopia: The snapshot lies in {path}. Take what you need, or put a folder back with «Restore…» of that folder.
errors.restore_busy_backup: A backup run holds the engine's lock — I bring nothing back until it is done.
errors.restore_busy_check: Mr. Backupsy is on his tour — I bring nothing back until he is done.
errors.restore_busy_dryrun: Mr. Backupsy is on a dry run — I bring nothing back until he is done.
errors.restore_busy_setup: Mr. Backupsy's setup holds the engine's lock — I bring nothing back until it is done.
errors.restore_busy_restore: A restore is going on ({what}) — one at a time.
errors.restore_busy_other: Someone holds the backup engine's lock — I bring nothing back until it is free.
errors.restore_changed: Something changed on the server since the preview — here is what would happen now.
errors.restore_stopped: The restore was stopped from outside (the server shut down?).
errors.restore_putback_not: There is nothing to put back.
errors.restore_putback_done: This restore was put back already.
errors.restore_aside_gone: What I put aside is no longer there: {path} — so I can't put it back.
errors.restore_file_odd: {path} is a link or a folder — I leave it alone.
errors.restore_db_name: The database's name in {file} is unusual — I won't use it in a command.
errors.restore_container_missing: The container {container} isn't on this server — restore its template or compose files first.
errors.restore_immich_folder: Immich only comes back into a fresh database, and its database folder can't be put aside ({why}).
errors.restore_asleep: The disk ({base}) is asleep — tick «wake» if you really need it.
errors.restore_wake_failed: I tried to wake the disk ({base}), but it didn't answer — I don't read it like this. Have a look at it on Unraid's Main page, then try again.
errors.restore_no_snapshot: No local snapshot holds this folder.
errors.restore_swap_mountpoint: {dataset} has a mountpoint of its own — I don't swap it; copying next to it works.
errors.restore_swap_inner: Datasets of their own lie inside it ({list}) — I don't swap it as a whole; copying next to it works.
errors.restore_swap_spread: The folder also lies on other disks (or on a sleeping one) — swapping only its part on {base} would leave a folder of two states. Copy it next to it instead.
errors.restore_exists: Already there: {path} — I never write over it.
errors.restore_share_missing: The share {share} isn't on this server. Create it first in Unraid (Shares → Add Share) — I never create a share myself.
errors.restore_no_user_shares: User shares are off (Settings → Global Share Settings) — I bring things back onto the share, through /mnt/user.
errors.restore_not_in_snapshot: This snapshot holds nothing of {path} — choose another one.
errors.restore_too_many: There are {n} entries at the top of the share — more than I bring back at once ({max}). Bring back single folders through Ms. Snapshotini or Kopia.
errors.restore_nothing_chosen: Nothing is ticked — choose what comes back.
errors.restore_vm_running: {name} is not shut off ({state}) — shut it down first; I never force anything off.
errors.restore_vm_uses: The VM {name} is running ({state}) and keeps its disk here: {path} — shut it down first (Unraid → VMs); I never stop a VM myself.
errors.restore_vm_service_off: The VM service is off — switch it on (Settings → VM Manager) so libvirt can take the configuration.
errors.restore_config_same: Everything is the same on the server as in the package — nothing to restore.
errors.restore_kopia_stopped: The Kopia container {name} is stopped — start it first.
errors.restore_kopia_root: I don't know under which path the Kopia container sees the snapshots — Mr. Backupsy's next tour tells me.
errors.restore_kopia_no_mapping: The Kopia container {name} has no writable folder for restores — see «Restoring with me» under Kopia.
dbs_sub: Every database dump and every media server's database copy in the apps' packages, per app — when it was made and where it is kept. «Restore…» first shows exactly what would happen.
dbs_none: No database dumps or copies in the packages. Which databases Mr. Backupsy dumps is decided in his «Set up…»; media servers that keep running get copies of their databases.
dbs.name: {engine} · {name}
dbs.by_hand_text: Stop the app's other containers first — only the database container runs. The command plays the dump in and overwrites what the database holds now, with the user and password variables the dump was made with. «Restore…» does the same, with a safety dump of what is there first.
dbs.earlier_none: No other copy of it in the snapshots of the backup place — only the one above.
help.dbs_text: Every database dump and media server's database copy in the packages, per app: the database (a MariaDB dump holds one database, Postgres and MongoDB the whole server; a media server's SQLite copies go back together), its container, the size, the night it was made and where its package is kept. A click on a row unfolds its files, the way by hand and earlier nights; «Restore…» opens the same preview as in the app's row.
